children: SoftBank Group Corp. is seeking more than $11 billion equivalent in bonds, Bloomberg reported, citing people familiar with the matter, in what would be one of the largest junk bond deals ever by a single firm outside a distressed exchange. The plan is $10 billion of dollar notes across three tenors and 1 billion of euro notes across two. Proceeds partly fund a follow-on OpenAI investment expected to close next month.

SoftBank has committed close to $65 billion to OpenAI and has been raising debt on multiple fronts at once. It closed last week with nearly $21 billion of fresh potential borrowing: a $5 billion increase to its Arm
backed margin loan, taking that facility to $25 billion, and $450 million added to an existing credit line, now $6.5 billion. Apollo Global Management Inc.

is discussing raising a separate loan to SoftBank by $3.6 billion to $9 billion, on top of an $11.87 billion loan secured this month. It has sold almost $15 billion of notes across currencies this year, the most of any junk-rated borrower.

SoftBank's 2031 dollar bond yield climbed to 8.2% this month from as low as 6.7% in January. The cost to insure its debt against default hit a three-year high as concerns about an AI slowdown intensified, after Anthropic's Dario Amodei and other AI leaders called for slowing model development. SoftBank carries a BB+ rating from S&P, its highest speculative grade, against AA+ and AA for Alphabet
, the two largest corporate bond issuers of 2026.

title: SoftBank Seeks $11 Billion in What Would Be a Record Junk Bond Sale
